description: DEF CON 32 App Sec Village focuses on application security, secure software development, and modern API and cloud vulnerabilities. The talks cover topics ranging from CI/CD pipeline exploitation and LLM application security to frontend defenses and vulnerability management.

talks.title: AppSec Considerations from the Casino Industry
talks.teaser: Examines ransomware attacks against casino giants like MGM and Caesars, highlighting application vulnerabilities and ICT and IoT security challenges.
talks.summary:
Ransomware Threats in the Casino Industry

The casino and gaming industry has experienced a surge of high-profile ransomware attacks that create unprecedented operational and financial disruptions. Compromised applications and connected systems directly threaten customer data security, gaming operations, and regulatory compliance.

Case Studies of Major Casino Breaches

Examining recent incidents at industry operators like MGM and Caesars highlights how malicious actors target application layer vulnerabilities. The attacks demonstrate the critical interplay between information and communications technology (ICT), IoT devices on the casino floor, and underlying enterprise application security.

talks.title: Web2 Meets Web3: Hacking Decentralized Applications
talks.teaser: Real-world attack vectors, threat modeling techniques, and vulnerability case studies for penetration testing decentralized Web3 applications.
talks.summary:
Architecture and Attack Surface of Dapps

Decentralized applications (Dapps) combine conventional Web2 frontend and backend components with blockchain-based smart contracts. This hybrid architecture introduces unique security challenges that span both traditional application weaknesses and blockchain-specific attack vectors.

Threat Modeling and Vulnerability Case Studies

Threat modeling for Dapps requires evaluating the trust boundaries between off-chain Web2 interfaces and on-chain state. Real-world vulnerability case studies demonstrate how attackers exploit flaws in Dapp integration points, access control, and transaction workflows.

talks.title: Your CI/CD Pipeline Is Vulnerable, But It's Not Your Fault
talks.teaser: Demonstrates a command injection vulnerability in the Bazel GitHub Action that allowed malicious tampering in Google's build pipeline.
talks.summary:
Command Injection in CI/CD Workflows

CI/CD pipelines frequently execute untrusted input within automation runners, creating high-impact attack surfaces. A single vulnerable pipeline component can allow attackers to achieve arbitrary command execution within build environments.

Compromising the Bazel GitHub Action

Research into Google's open-source Bazel project uncovered a command injection vulnerability in its GitHub Actions workflow. Attackers could exploit this flaw to execute unauthorized code during pipeline execution and tamper with repository release artifacts.

Securing Pipeline Runners

Defending CI/CD infrastructure requires strict input sanitization, least-privilege token permissions, and isolation of untrusted pull request triggers to prevent repository compromise.

talks.title: Lessons Learned from Building & Defending LLM Applications
talks.teaser: Practical insights and defensive strategies from real-world development and hardening of production LLM applications.
talks.summary:
Challenges in Securing LLM Applications

Deploying large language models into production introduces new vulnerability classes alongside traditional application security challenges. Securing AI applications requires moving beyond theoretical threat models to address real-world operational edge cases.

Vulnerability Patterns and Defense Strategies

Critical risks in LLM architectures include untrusted context injection, unauthorized tool execution, and insecure data retrieval pipelines. Implementing defensive guardrails, rigorous input validation, and output filtering strengthens application robustness against adversarial exploitation.

talks.title: Using EPSS for Better Vulnerability Management
talks.teaser: How the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) uses threat data and probability modeling to prioritize patching across pipelines and systems.
talks.summary:
The Exploit Prediction Scoring System

Traditional vulnerability scoring often fails to reflect whether a flaw will actually be targeted in the wild. The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) provides a data-driven model that calculates the probability of real-world exploitation using live threat telemetry and CVE metadata.

Integrating EPSS into Pipelines and Patching

Applying EPSS scores within CI/CD pipelines and vulnerability management programs allows security teams to prioritize remediation based on actual threat likelihood rather than static severity scores alone.

talks.title: Speed Bumps and Speed Hacks: Adventures in Car Mfg Security
talks.teaser: Vulnerability chaining and web application research uncovering flaws across eleven major automotive manufacturers.
talks.summary:
Application Security in Automotive Manufacturing

While automotive physical safety receives intense scrutiny, the web applications and backend portals operated by car manufacturers frequently suffer from classic security weaknesses. Research across eleven major car brands revealed widespread exposure of sensitive customer and corporate data.

Chaining Web Vulnerabilities

Attack demonstrations show how unpatched third-party software and traditional web vulnerabilities can be chained together to compromise manufacturer infrastructure and leak personal identifiable information (PII).

Responsible Disclosure Outcomes

Coordinated disclosure across multiple automotive enterprises highlights the value of formal vulnerability disclosure programs for remediating systemic supply chain and application flaws.

talks.title: Securing Frontends at Scale: Paving Our Way to Post-XSS World
talks.teaser: Google's engineering blueprint for eliminating cross-site scripting at scale using compile-time and runtime frontend protections.
talks.summary:
Evolving Beyond Cross-Site Scripting

Cross-site scripting (XSS) remains one of the most persistent classes of web application vulnerabilities. Eliminating XSS across massive codebases requires systemic architectural defenses rather than relying solely on developer vigilance.

Compile-Time and Runtime Protections at Google

Google implemented integrated compile-time type enforcement and runtime sanitization mechanisms across hundreds of products serving billions of users. These automated guardrails prevent injection flaws by design while maintaining developer productivity.

Lessons for Large-Scale Frontend Defense

Deploying scalable frontend security frameworks provides key insights into API design, deprecation strategies, and the technical roadmap toward a post-XSS web platform.

talks.title: Defeating Secure Code Review GPT Hallucinations
talks.teaser: Analysis of when and why large language models hallucinate during automated code review, and how misleading identifier names induce errors.
talks.summary:
LLMs in Automated Code Analysis

Large language models are increasingly used for code security analysis tasks including semantic code search, vulnerability detection, and code clone analysis. However, their probabilistic nature introduces significant risks of false positives and hallucinated conclusions.

Mechanisms of Review Hallucinations

Empirical testing shows that popular LLMs rely heavily on semantic variable and function naming conventions rather than true control-flow and data-flow semantics. Misleading or obfuscated identifier names consistently induce incorrect security assessments.

Mitigating AI Code Review Pitfalls

Understanding failure modes in LLM-assisted code review enables security engineers to design hybrid validation pipelines combining AI heuristics with deterministic static analysis tools.

talks.title: The Immortal Retrofuturism of Mainframes and How to Keep Them Safe
talks.teaser: Architecture, operational role, and defensive controls for securing modern enterprise mainframe environments supporting mission-critical banking.
talks.summary:
The Modern Role of Mainframes

Mainframe technology remains the core compute backbone for global financial transactions, airline reservations, and critical enterprise infrastructure. Despite perceptions of being legacy hardware, modern mainframes process massive transaction volumes with extreme reliability and uptime.

Mainframe Architecture and Enterprise Topology

Understanding how mainframes integrate with modern cloud and distributed architectures is essential for securing critical business data paths. The session explores attack surfaces unique to mainframe environments and how they connect to outward-facing applications.

Defensive Strategies for Mainframe Environments

Securing mainframe systems requires specialized access controls, continuous integrity monitoring, and integrating mainframe telemetry into centralized security operations centers (SOCs).

talks.title: The Darkest Side of Bug Bounty
talks.teaser: Unvarnished perspective on the systemic friction, triage dynamics, and economic realities of commercial bug bounty platforms.
talks.summary:
Dynamics of the Bug Bounty Ecosystem

Bug bounty programs operate as a multi-party marketplace connecting independent researchers, client security teams, and platform intermediaries. This complex dynamic frequently creates misaligned incentives and communication breakdowns.

Unspoken Realities and Program Friction

An analysis from the perspectives of hacker, program manager, and platform operator exposes common pitfalls including duplicate disputes, scope ambiguity, triage delays, and mediation challenges.

Navigating and Improving the Tri-Party Relationship

Actionable strategies help bug hunters manage expectations and protect their time, while guiding program owners toward fairer triage policies and sustainable researcher relationships.

talks.title: Relative Path File Injection: The Next Evolution in RPO
talks.teaser: Exploits URL path handling differentials to turn trusted websites into malware delivery platforms using Relative Path File Injection.
talks.summary:
From Relative Path Overwrite to File Injection

While traditional Relative Path Overwrite (RPO) attacks manipulate browser path resolution to inject styles, Relative Path File Injection (RPFI) extends this technique to file downloads. Attackers abuse discrepancies between web specifications and browser URL parsing to trick users into downloading malicious payloads from trusted domains.

Anatomy of an RPFI Attack

The attack vector combines polyglot file constructs with relative path manipulation, allowing benign endpoints to return attacker-controlled executable content. Demonstrations illustrate how innocent-looking links on trusted websites can be weaponized for malware delivery.

Detection and Mitigation Strategies

Identifying RPFI vulnerabilities requires auditing how applications handle dynamic path resolution and strict enforcement of download content types. Open-source proof-of-concept tooling aids in scanning for vulnerable path handling implementations.

talks.title: Ticking SQLi
talks.teaser: Exploration of time-based blind SQL injection techniques and data extraction strategies through the lens of Operation GhostShell.
talks.summary:
Mechanics of Time-Based Blind SQLi

Time-based SQL injection allows attackers to extract database records from blind endpoints by forcing conditional time delays within SQL queries. This technique bypasses traditional error-handling and out-of-band detection controls by relying purely on response timing.

Operation GhostShell Case Study

An analysis of historic breaches from Operation GhostShell illustrates how attackers systematically enumerated and exfiltrated sensitive databases from major universities using time-delay vectors.

Detection and Prevention Techniques

Defending against blind SQL injection requires moving away from dynamic query concatenation to parameterized queries, prepared statements, and rigorous database user permission scoping.

talks.title: Transforming AppSec: Protecting 'Everything as Code'
talks.teaser: Modernizing application security programs to protect infrastructure-as-code, secrets, and emerging cloud and AI technology stacks.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Application Security

Rapid adoption of cloud computing, microservices, mobile platforms, and generative AI has expanded the traditional scope of AppSec. Security practices have shifted from point-in-time SAST and DAST scans toward continuous, proactive defense across the entire software development lifecycle.

Securing Everything as Code

As infrastructure, pipelines, and configurations are codified into software repositories, securing Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and enforcing automated secret management become essential to preventing widespread cloud compromise.

Building a Holistic AppSec Posture

Modern AppSec teams must integrate real-time anomaly detection, rigorous configuration validation, and developer-first security tooling to manage risk across complex hybrid environments.

talks.title: 0.0.0.0 Day: Exploiting Localhost APIs from the Browser
talks.teaser: Unveils the 0.0.0.0-day vulnerability in major browsers that lets public websites pivot to internal localhost APIs and achieve RCE.
talks.summary:
The 0.0.0.0-Day Vulnerability

While browsers enforce same-origin policies to isolate web origins, a systemic flaw in major browsers allowed public internet websites to send requests to IP address 0.0.0.0, bypassing standard localhost restrictions.

Attacking Internal Developer Services

By sending HTTP requests to local ports via 0.0.0.0, malicious web pages can interact directly with unauthenticated services and developer tools running on a developer's workstation behind corporate firewalls.

Remote Code Execution Demonstration

A live attack demonstration showcases how the 0.0.0.0-day enables remote code execution against popular data engineering and AI development frameworks by exploiting unauthenticated local management APIs.

talks.title: BOLABuster: Harnessing LLMs for Automating BOLA Detection
talks.teaser: Automated detection of Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) vulnerabilities across web APIs using LLMs in BOLABuster.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Automated BOLA Detection

Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) consistently ranks among the most critical API security flaws. Automated scanning for BOLA has traditionally been difficult because detecting authorization bypasses requires understanding stateful business logic and endpoint dependencies.

BOLABuster Architecture and LLM Integration

BOLABuster uses large language models to analyze API documentation and traffic flows, infer object relationships, generate context-aware test cases, and validate unauthorized access responses across user sessions.

Real-World Discoveries in Open Source

Testing BOLABuster against popular open-source platforms uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities, including fifteen CVEs in a single project and CVE-2024-1313 in Grafana.

talks.title: The Missing Link: How We Collect and Leverage SBOMs
talks.teaser: How Schneider Electric generates, stores, and operationalizes thousands of product SBOMs to accelerate CERT incident response.
talks.summary:
Operationalizing SBOMs at Scale

Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) provide visibility into software dependencies, but collecting and maintaining them across large enterprise product portfolios poses significant operational challenges.

Enterprise Implementation at Schneider Electric

Schneider Electric updated internal policies and automated tooling to generate, collect, and store thousands of product SBOMs. This centralized inventory enables the corporate Product CERT to rapidly pinpoint vulnerable components across product lines.

Incident Response During Major Disclosures

Real-world case studies during the Log4j and OpenSSL vulnerability events demonstrate how structured SBOM data cut triage times from weeks to hours, allowing rapid customer guidance and remediation.

talks.title: Got 99 Problems but Prompt Injection Ain't Watermelon
talks.teaser: Navigating the complexities of responsible vulnerability disclosure, data bias, and model manipulation in AI systems.
talks.summary:
Vulnerability Disclosure in Artificial Intelligence

Disclosing security flaws in artificial intelligence introduces distinct challenges compared to traditional software. Model non-determinism, proprietary weights, and data privacy complicate remediation and reproduction.

Data Bias and Model Manipulation

Security risks in AI extend beyond prompt injection to include data poisoning, training bias exploitation, and model tampering, which can systematically distort system outputs without triggering traditional alarms.

Building Standardized AI Disclosure Frameworks

Establishing transparent, responsible disclosure standards across AI vendors, security researchers, and regulatory bodies is essential for maintaining public trust and system integrity.

talks.title: Navigating the Cyber Security Labyrinth: Choose Your Own Security Adventure
talks.teaser: Practical strategies for solo AppSec engineers navigating burnout, team layoffs, and expanding threat landscapes.
talks.summary:
Pressures Facing AppSec Practitioners

Recent industry trends including workforce reductions, increased attack velocity, and expanding compliance requirements have placed intense strain on application security professionals, frequently leading to burnout.

Operating as a Solo AppSec Engineer

Solo practitioners and small security teams face the challenge of prioritizing competing demands across vulnerability remediation, code reviews, and stakeholder management with limited resources.

Strategies for Sustainable Security Operations

Establishing clear risk boundaries, automating repetitive workflows, and focusing on high-leverage defensive controls enable practitioners to deliver effective security while preventing exhaustion.

talks.title: Maturing Your Application Security Program
talks.teaser: A practical three-tier maturity model for evolving application security programs beyond intimidating compliance frameworks.
talks.summary:
Demystifying AppSec Maturity Models

Standard security maturity frameworks often present overwhelming requirements that discourage teams in the early stages of building an application security program.

Three Stages of Program Maturity

Drawing on experience across hundreds of organizations, the session outlines three distinct phases of AppSec evolution, from ad-hoc vulnerability patching to structured tooling and proactive developer empowerment.

Actionable Steps for Progression

Practical guidance focuses on incremental improvements, establishing developer security champions, integrating baseline automation, and measuring measurable risk reduction.

talks.title: Gridlock: The Dual Edged Sword of EV and Solar APIs in Grid Security
talks.teaser: How API vulnerabilities in EV chargers and solar inverters create systemic risks for power grid infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Interconnected Grid and Renewable APIs

The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EV) charging networks and photovoltaic (PV) solar inverters has linked millions of distributed energy assets to centralized cloud APIs and the electrical grid.

Vulnerabilities in Distributed Energy Management

Industry rush-to-market pressures have resulted in widespread authentication flaws, authorization bypasses, and insecure endpoints in solar inverter and charging management platforms.

Systemic Grid Disruption Risks

Attack simulations demonstrate how coordinated manipulation of aggregated power loads through vulnerable APIs could destabilize regional power grid frequency and trigger widespread blackouts.

talks.title: Fine Grained Authorisation with Relationship Based Access Control
talks.teaser: Implementing scalable fine-grained authorization using Relationship-Based Access Control (ReBAC) without hardcoded business logic.
talks.summary:
Limits of Traditional Authorization

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) struggle to model complex, graph-like permissions such as nested resource hierarchies and social connections without cluttering application code.

Principles of Relationship-Based Access Control

Relationship-Based Access Control (ReBAC) formalizes authorization as a graph of subjects, relations, and objects, enabling dynamic evaluation of complex permissions like transitive ownership and shared folder inheritance.

Deploying Fine-Grained Authorization Services

Live demonstrations show how to define relationship schemas and deploy dedicated authorization engines that decouple access control decisions from core application business logic.

talks.title: Hacking Corporate Banking for Fun and Profit
talks.teaser: Reconnaissance and vulnerability discovery across enterprise banking software used by major financial institutions worldwide.
talks.summary:
Targeting Widely Deployed Banking Software

Security research initiated during a financial sector bug bounty engagement uncovered third-party corporate banking software deployed across dozens of major banks worldwide.

Reconnaissance and Attack Surface Mapping

Analyzing client marketing materials, client-side application bundles, and undocumented API endpoints revealed extensive hidden attack surfaces and administrative interfaces.

Exploitation and Vulnerability Discovery

Detailed findings demonstrate how SQL injection vulnerabilities and access control bypasses within the platform allowed unauthorized extraction of sensitive financial data and privilege escalation.

talks.title: Engineers & Exploits: The Quest for Security
talks.teaser: Spyros Gasteratos and Andra Lezza explore strategies for integrating security into the product development lifecycle through threat modeling, OWASP Cornucopia, and collaborative developer workflows.
talks.summary:
Integrating Security into the Product Lifecycle

Security is often treated as an afterthought in software engineering, leading to friction between security architects and development teams. Fostering early collaboration and establishing shared mental models helps embed security directly into developer workflows rather than imposing late-stage blockers.

Practical Threat Modeling with OWASP Cornucopia

Utilizing lightweight threat modeling frameworks like OWASP Cornucopia allows engineering teams to identify actionable security user stories. By balancing mitigation workloads with business context, development organizations can achieve measurable security by design without derailing sprint velocity.
